name: Publius
overview: Publius is a male figure identified as the leading man of the island of Malta, as recorded in Acts 28:7. No tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided about him. His role indicates a position of authority on the island during the time of the Apostle Paul's visit.
namesAndTitles: The name Publius is the only recorded name for this individual, and no specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to it in the biblical text. It is simply presented as a proper name in Acts 28:7.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Publius beyond his role as the leading man of Malta. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Publius holds significance in the biblical narrative as a prominent local leader who interacted with the Apostle Paul during his time on Malta. His position as the island's chief man highlights the early spread of the gospel beyond traditional Jewish and Roman centers, demonstrating God's providence in placing Paul under the care of a local authority. This encounter underscores the theme of divine orchestration in the advancement of the Christian mission.
